articles.title_orig: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
articles.title_zh: Ukraine strikes Putin’s prized Crimean bridge for third time in a week
articles.content_orig:
Russian president makes remarks after Ukraine strikes strategic bridge to Crimea for third time in a week
Vladimir Putin has said Russia’s response to the bombing of the Kerch bridge to Crimea will be “painful”, after Ukraine attacked the strategic connection for the third time this week.
The warning was delivered at a press conference after Putin met Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China. The Russian president claimed he had been considering agreeing to local ceasefires until the Kerch road bridge was destroyed.
“After the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, we will not negotiate,” Putin said, insisting the bridge was used only by civilians. “We will respond to these attacks. Our response will be far more painful than Kyiv’s attack on the bridge.”
A series of explosions were heard in the Ukrainian capital in the mid-afternoon, and there were reports that a Russian drone had struck near the Dutch embassy in Kyiv, though it was unclear if it was deliberately targeted.
Shortly after midnight on Tuesday, Ukraine’s military blew up the central span of the Kerch road bridge in a complex air raid that involved Ruta cruise missiles made by a Dutch company as well as several Ukrainian cruise missiles and drones.
Russia threatened the Netherlands afterwards, with the Russian embassy in the country asking: “Is the Dutch government openly taking part in the conflict?” after the company, Destinus, had said it was a key element in the attack.
Tom Berendsen, the Dutch foreign minister, confirmed that “a projectile struck behind” the embassy in Kyiv. “Fortunately, our colleagues are unharmed, though there is some minor damage to the building,” he said, adding that officials were now investigating the incident.
A 26-year-old man had been killed and five others injured in the afternoon attacks, city authorities said.
Ukrainian military sources said the destruction of the Kerch bridge had been deliberately timed to embarrass Putin before the extraordinary summit , in which the Russian president sat down with Trump and Xi to discuss the war and other issues.
After his talks with Putin, Trump dialled into a meeting of Ukraine’s European allies in Berlin, during which he reportedly asked why European countries continued to spend billions on military support for Kyiv and said Putin was ready to negotiate a peace deal.
The British prime minister, Andy Burnham, when asked at a press conference whether Trump was painting too optimistic a picture of Russia’s desire for peace, said: “Too rosy a picture? No, certainly not. That was not the phone call that we heard from the president this afternoon. I would say quite the opposite, to be honest.”
Ukraine followed up Tuesday’s bombing of the Kerch bridge with a further attack on the remaining rail bridge to Crimea on Wednesday night. Train services were halted as a result of the strikes, which Ukraine’s military said were conducted with Neptune missiles made in Ukraine.
Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, said on Wednesday night that there had been another attack on the bridge, then added on Thursday that trains would start crossing from “approximately 4pm”.
Emergency repair workers had made “heroic efforts” to restore the track, the governor said. Nobody was reported wounded as a result of the incident, Russia’s transport ministry added.
Ukraine’s military said the Kerch bridge was “the main land artery the Russian army uses to supply its occupation groupings in the south with fuel, ammunition and equipment” – in contrast to the comments made by Putin.
The $3.6bn (£2.7bn) bridge, built by Russia after its occupation of Crimea, has been struck three times in a week. Initial attacks on Monday had shown that Tuesday’s full-scale assault would be possible.
A 227-metre section of the road spanning the Kerch strait collapsed into the Sea of Azov after a complex air raid that had been prepared and planned over several weeks.
A source in Ukraine’s armed forces said this week’s attacks were designed to embarrass Putin on the world stage. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” they said.
For Ukraine, the bridge across the Kerch strait is a hated symbol of Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Ukraine has previously declared that the bridge, built eight years ago, is illegal. Kyiv had tried to blow it up twice in the past – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.
Zelesnkyy described the earlier attack this week as the culmination of a seven-stage campaign to demolish the bridge, largely involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles, clearing the radar and air defences of Russian-occupied Ukraine.
Flamingo FP-5 cruise missiles and Palianytsia drones struck the central section of the bridge, bringing down its supporting arch.

articles.title_orig: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.title_zh: Stocks making the biggest moves Thursday: Palo Alto Networks, Take-Two Interactive, Everpure, Walmart & more
articles.content_orig:
Palo Alto Networks popped in early trading Thursday, boosted by quarterly results that beat analyst expectations. AMD, meanwhile, tumbled on the back of a short seller report.
Follow along as CNBC covers the biggest stock market moves of the day.
Neocloud CoreWeave gained 1% on enthusiasm from the Anthropic IPO plus a change in Texas permitting that favors data center development.
Texas officials started issuing air permits again for data center construction projects, according to Reuters , which bodes well for the future of the physical component of the AI buildout.
Nvidia's highly anticipated earnings call earlier this week also offered clarity on the leadership direction for the firm, which Wall Street analysts responded positively to. Analysts at Truist were encouraged on Tuesday by Nvidia statements on the call about its relationship to neoclouds.
"Notably, NVIDIA's earnings commentary … [described] neoclouds as an 'increasingly important' part of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem and stating that it will continue working with and supporting leading neocloud partners, while becoming more disciplined and selective in that support."
AMD shares tumbled more than 9% after Hunterbrook Capital revealed it took a short position on the company.
In a post titled "AMD has its own China problem", Hunterbrook alleges that "AMD firmware keeps turning up at a blacklisted Chinese company and three companies tied to it, just as U.S. export restrictions are scheduled to expand."
"AMD, which bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong, also depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips," Hunterbrook added.
CNBC reached out to AMD for comment.
Shares of Coherent are up nearly 11%, extending gains after Nvidia 's latest earnings report earlier in the week highlighted continued demand for data-center technology.
Coherent, which supplies optical components used in AI data centers, said its data-center revenue rose 85% year over year in its fiscal first quarter.
On Nov. 18, the company's board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $2 billion . Coherent may buy shares in the open market or through other transactions. The program has no expiration date and does not require the company to repurchase a specific amount.
Shares of the software company making tools for computer chips jumped 3.2% after Barclays initiated coverage with an overweight rating and a $640 price target implying 47% upside from Wednesday's close. Analyst Saket Kalia noted that Synopsys is the leader of a growing Electronic Design Automation (EDA) market, which is driven by rising spend in semiconductor research and development.
MongoDB gained 4% before the bell following an upgrade at UBS to buy from neutral.
The bank's channel checks pointed to steady demand and better-than-expected consumer and partner growth, which should support durable 20%-plus total revenue growth and 25%-plus revenue growth for its cloud database service Atlas over the coming years, analyst Radi Sultan said.
In addition, MongoDB could be utilized in 20% to 40% of incremental AI workloads, which is not fully reflected in the stock's valuation, he said.
Data storage stocks are getting a lift in the premarket Thursday as the Anthropic IPO aims to breathe new life into AI-trade
Shares of Seagate Technology are up more than 6% while Western Digital stock popped 5.8%.
Seagate and Western Digital provide provide mass data storage infrastructure, a crucial role in the AI ecosystem to help AI models run.
The strong momentum around data storage and AI infrastructure demand is already high.
But a large chuck of that demand will come from leading AI lab Anthropic, which is set to go public Thursday.
Chipmakers advanced on Thursday ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
Marvell gained 4.2%, Advanced Micro Devices is up 2.8%, Broadcom advanced 2.5%, Intel moved 4.4% higher and Nvidia is up 1.5%.
These artificial intelligence chips will help Anthropic run Claude models faster.
Leading chipmakers need the IPO to go well, as Anthropic has $900 billion in spending commitments.
Shares of Bloom Energy surged nearly 8% in the premarket Thursday after being upgraded to outperform at BMO Capital Markets.
The analysts cited their endorsement of the company after coming away with positive meetings with management.
The firm however decreased its price target to $230 from $260, which still implies a 35% upside to the stock's Thursday close of $170 per share.
UBS upgraded the intelligent content management provider to buy from neutral, sending shares 3.6% higher in premarket trading.
The firm believes Box 's recent artificial intelligence growth acceleration can support sustained double-digit revenue growth. "Investors have been looking for evidence that AI can drive an inflection in software growth, and Box is increasingly demonstrating exactly that," analyst Taylor McGinnis wrote.
Walmart shares were down more than 1% even after the retail giant reported third-quarter results that beat expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 65 cents on revenue of $188.84 billion. Analysts expected a profit of 64 cents per share on revenue of $187.27 billion.
For the year, Walmart sees net sales rising 4.9% to 5.2%, more than a previous guidance of 4% to 5%.
Shares of Take-Two Interactive slipped 1%, giving back some of their gains from the previous session. The stock popped more than 6% on Wednesday ahead of the release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" game.
Take-Two is up nearly 14% in November, though the stock has dropped 15% in 2026.
Cybersecurity player Palo Alto Networks advanced 10% after its fiscal first-quarter results came in above the Street's expectations.
The company earned $1.05 per share on an adjusted basis and revenue of $3.44 billion. The LSEG consensus estimate called for 97 cents per share on $3.31 billion of revenue.
Guidance for the fiscal year ending July 2027 calls for adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share on revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion. Analysts sought $4.18 per share and $14.16 billion, according to LSEG.
The data management company advanced 5% after raising its guidance for the fiscal-year ending January 2027.
Everpure sees revenue in a range of $5.20 billion to $5.21 billion, up from its earlier call of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for $5.06 billion.
Third-quarter results also surpassed estimates on the top and bottom lines.
The manufacturer of power generation equipment pulled back 1%. Woodward expects adjusted earnings for the fiscal year ending September 2027 to range between $10.20 and $10.70 per share, below the FactSet consensus estimate of $10.74 per share.

articles.title_orig: China and Russia say they and US agree on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, dialogue on nuclear
articles.title_zh: China and Russia say they and US agree on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, dialogue on nuclear
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his trilateral meeting Thursday with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin , although his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.
Trump has been pushing for China to join the U.S. and Russia in a new nuclear arms control agreement since his first term in office. Still, he has sought to limit expectations for any major progress in Shenzhen, China, where the world’s top three nuclear powers are meeting on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders .
Russia suspended its participation in New START, its last remaining nuclear arms pact with the U.S., when it invaded Ukraine in 2022, denying inspections of its nuclear sites. Ahead of the treaty’s expiration this past February , Russia said it would keep to the deal’s limitations on its arsenal for another year, but Trump insisted a new agreement must include China and possibly other nuclear powers.
China has said an arms control agreement should remain between the U.S. and Russia, which together hold nearly 90% of the world’s nuclear arsenal with more than 5,000 warheads each. China has about 600, according to Pentagon estimates, though by 2030 it could have up to 1,000 if its arsenal continues to expand at the current rate.
“China is building up its nuclear arsenal to a very significant degree, and it will continue to do so, and wants to continue to do so,” David Sacks, a senior fellow for Asia studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told reporters Wednesday.
The Chinese foreign ministry has declined to say whether nuclear arms control will be discussed at the trilateral meeting on Thursday, with spokesperson Mao Ning saying earlier this week that the three leaders “will have an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace.”
In a call last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi “agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization,” according to a U.S. readout of the call. The Chinese readout made no reference to such a discussion.
Trump has admitted that it will be difficult to get Russia and China to consider reducing their nuclear arsenals.
“So we’re going to talk about denuclearization. Tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes, right? But especially since you do have other countries,” he said Monday. “But we’re going to be talking about denuclearization.”
Even in the hours leading up to this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, the world’s top two nuclear powers were making shows of force. On Tuesday, the U.S. launched an unarmed intercontinental ballistic missile in a previously unannounced test at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. Hours later, Russia landed two strategic bombers in Vietnam to coincide with Putin’s arrival in China.
While one meeting is not likely to produce dramatic breakthroughs, it could kickstart a process that leads to sustained, formal bilateral or multilateral negotiations on nuclear risk reduction, arms control and disarmament, said Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Washington-based Arms Control Association.
“A top priority for all three leaders should be to head off a costly, escalatory nuclear arms race involving the further buildup of nuclear forces and the resumption of nuclear testing by any state,” he said.
Da Wei, director of the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, said nuclear arms control was not a “proper topic” for the trilateral meeting given the complexity of the issue and how little time Trump, Putin and Xi will have together.
But if the three leaders “can say something about nuclear stability, like a nuclear war is not winnable and should not be fought, I think that will be helpful,” he said in an interview Wednesday.
Rubio has acknowledged that a new agreement could take some time.
“Past agreements, including New START, took years to negotiate and were built upon decades of precedent. They were also between two powers, not three or more,” he wrote on Substack in February. “However, just because something is hard does not mean we should not pursue it or settle for less.”
Abigail Williams is a producer and reporter for NBC News covering the State Department.

articles.title_orig: Trump: ‘We spy on China, they spy on us’
articles.title_zh: Trump: ‘We spy on China, they spy on us’
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
SHENZHEN, China — President Trump has begun an extraordinary visit to Shenzhen, where he is set to join the leaders of Russia and China — two of Washington’s principal geopolitical rivals — for an unprecedented trilateral summit Thursday.
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed Trump on the tarmac upon his arrival, reciprocating a rare honor Trump extended to him during his September visit to Washington.
All three leaders attended a dinner alongside other regional heads of government on Wednesday night, participating in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, known as APEC.
The trilateral meeting will be the first of its kind by leaders of the United States, Russia and China, three nations with the world’s largest nuclear arsenals.
But while Trump has embraced a strategy of diplomatic engagement with historic foes, the three leaders enter the meeting with starkly different agendas.
Russian President Vladimir Putin hopes to secure space and time to continue executing his war against Ukraine. Trump says he would like to discuss a nuclear arms control agreement and his war in Iran. And Xi aims to present China as a superpower on the international stage, capable of forging world peace.
Meeting with Putin before Trump arrived, Xi said that China’s relationship with Russia had remained as steadfast “as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two sides, he said, would pursue a “multipolar world” — a vision for a global balance of power that would see American influence weakened across Europe and Asia.
A new rule tightening loopholes in U.S. export controls sends a dual message to Beijing ahead of Thursday’s summit.
Trump, for his part, has hedged on his expectations of the summit, signaling resolve against China ahead of his arrival here.
On Monday, the Trump administration tightened export controls on semiconductor chips essential to artificial intelligence development, closing loopholes aimed at curbing Chinese efforts to circumvent restrictions — a move that Trump acknowledged might be an “insult” to Xi before the meeting.

Trump also met in Manila on Tuesday with fellow members of the Quad — India, Japan and Australia — in a show of resolve toward Beijing.
“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in the Philippines.
“We continue to protect peace through strength,” he added.
